feedback.problem:
$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{5}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+3\,k).
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given above. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=$
{{field-1}}
$i\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{5}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+3\,k)) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(-4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)\,k) \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{4}{5}‖\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j‖ \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{4}{5}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)}{\frac{4}{5}} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}
$$
